title: Cold rebuild: PUT with a version check
summary: Rebuild PUT with a version check from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **PUT with a version check** in *Concurrency tokens*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Which line makes EF compare the UPDATE with the version the **client** loaded?
steps.explain: The WHERE of the UPDATE uses the token's original value. Setting the current value instead would write the client's version into the row and compare with the one just read.

steps.title: Rebuild PUT with a version check cold
prompt: Write the whole bookings API again: `TicketsDb` with `Data Source=bookings.db` created at start-up, `POST /bookings` (version 1), `GET /bookings/{id}`, and `PUT /bookings/{id}` with body `{ "note", "version" }` that compares with the client's version, bumps it, answers 200, 409 on `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`, or 404.
`Booking`: `Id`, `Note`, `[ConcurrencyCheck] int Version`. All calls async with `ct`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
